Definition: from G575 and G906; to throw off; figuratively, to lose:--cast away.
BiblicalUsage: To throw off, to cast away. Hebrews 10:35 commands it of confidence — cast not away your confidence, which hath great recompence of reward — while blind Bartimaeus does it with his garment in Mark 10:50, casting it away and rising to come to Jesus. Romans 13:12 turns the same word on our old life: let us cast off the works of darkness and put on the armour of light.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the word teaches me what to drop and what to keep. The garment, the darkness — those I throw off gladly. But confidence in God is the one thing I must not cast away, because the reward attached to it is greater than anything my hands are holding.
